sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gabhair was an Irish mythological site. Sources also call it Gavra or Gowra. It may be a plain near Garristown in County Dublin. A great battle there broke the power of the Fianna. Those warriors followed the hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill. They had grown arrogant and troublesome. High King Cairbre Cinn-Chait sought to end their hold on the land. He won the battle but lost his life. Oscar, the grandson of Fionn, killed him. Oscar also died in the same fight.

okr.objective: Record Gabhair as the site of the Fianna's final defeat.
key_results: Locate Gabhair as a plain near Garristown in County Dublin.
Name the Fianna and their leader Fionn Mac Cumhaill.
Describe High King Cairbre Cinn-Chait's death at the hand of Oscar.
